create.name: Providence Zen Center
create.bio:
Providence Zen Center serves as the main temple for the Americas region of the Kwan Um School of Zen, the international community founded by the Korean Zen Master Seung Sahn. It grew out of the small group that formed around him after he arrived in Providence, Rhode Island, in 1972, and later moved to a wooded property in Cumberland, a short drive north of the city, where a pagoda and a monastery building now stand beside a pond. Its guiding teachers are Zen Master Dae Kwang, Zen Master Tan Gong (José Ramírez) and the abbot, Kwan Haeng Sunim.

Practice follows the Kwan Um forms of sitting, chanting, bowing and kong-an interviews with a teacher. The centre keeps a daily schedule, a free Wednesday evening dinner and practice, and a Sunday morning programme with a beginners' class and a Dharma talk that is also streamed. Several evenings a week run on Zoom. It holds one- to three-day retreats through the year and the long silent Kyol Che retreats in winter and summer, and offers guest stays and a residential training programme for those who want to live in a Zen community.

courses.title: Kyol Che Long Retreats
courses.description: The school's intensive silent retreats, held at the head temple for up to 90 days in winter and 30 days in summer, with set entry and exit dates. Earlier retreat experience in the Kwan Um School is required.

courses.title: Guest Stays
courses.description: Short or longer stays at the centre in shared or single rooms, joining the daily round of chanting and sitting. Breakfast is included; a monthly single-room option is also offered.
courses.price: Monthly Guest Stay – Single Room: $1,800/month; nightly rates on the page

courses.title: Zen Training Program (residency)
courses.description: Residents live, eat, work and practise together on the centre's schedule, following Seung Sahn's view that shared community life shows us our habits clearly. The monthly fee covers board and all retreats held there, including Kyol Che.

free_resources.title: Weekly Meditation Classes and Sunday Dharma Program
free_resources.description: A free beginners' instruction class on Wednesday evenings and Sunday mornings, followed by sitting and walking meditation and, on Sundays, a Dharma talk with questions. Donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Hybrid & Online Zen Practice
free_resources.description: Sunday sittings and talks, Tuesday chanting with kong-an interviews and a Thursday reading group, all joinable on Zoom, with the Sunday talk also streamed on YouTube.
